data.summary: Personal vs project constraints: user preferences recorded as constraints leak into every teammate's prime
data.detail: Colton (2026-09-15): users record personal preferences as constraints, and constraints are project-wide — prime's Active Constraints section shows every constraint to everyone regardless of who recorded it. Needs a personal/project split so a person's preferences apply only to them. Not built in v0.41.0 and no prior plan found in the graph. Per-person journal shards (v0.41.0) store who wrote each entry but the replayed graph is shared, so shards alone do not scope visibility. Open design questions: how scope is marked (field on constraint vs new node type), default for existing constraints, whether personal constraints are visible to teammates in search, how the recording agent decides scope.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal constraints rulings (Colton, 2026-09-15): constraints default to personal; teammates cannot find another person's personal constraints; agent judges scope by guidance and asks the human when unsure
data.detail: Personal preferences recorded as constraints were leaking into every teammate's prime and search. Ruling: a constraint defaults to personal (applies only to its recorder, by recorded_by email) unless it is true for anyone in the repo; the tool and skill carry guidance for judging, and the agent asks the human when unsure. Personal constraints are hidden from teammates across prime, search, node/neighbor lookups, dashboard and curation — not merely labeled. Rejected: labeled-but-visible (teammates' agents could still obey them) and a new preference node type. Known limit: hidden through the plugin, but still readable in the owner's committed journal file.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal constraints rulings round 2 (Colton, 2026-09-15): existing constraints stay project with no review prompt; only constraints can be personal; owner-only visibility, managers excluded
data.detail: Existing unscoped constraints stay project forever and owners reclassify by hand (rejected: owner review prompt, and bulk-converting to personal, which would hide real project rules like API limits). Personal scope applies to constraints only (rejected: patterns, which are usually shared conventions). Only the recorder can see or change a personal constraint (rejected: manager read access, which adds a roster-dependent leak path).
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Loss reporting leaked hidden node ids: journal_watch and rebuild loss checks computed from the raw graph, so a teammate's personal constraint id could surface in get_status.rehydrate_events and the session-start WARNING
data.detail: A viewer filter at storage read methods does not cover code that reads self._graph directly. Fix: the recorded known-ids snapshot and rebuild before-set hold only viewer-visible ids, while "missing" is computed against the FULL graph, so a hidden node still present is never falsely reported lost and a vanished teammate node is never named. Any future loss/diagnostic surface must use storage.visible_node_ids(), not graph.nodes.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: v0.42.0 built: personal vs project constraints — personal by default, hidden from teammates at one storage choke point
data.detail: Colton raised that users record preferences as constraints, which leaked to every teammate. Rulings: default personal with judging guidance and ask-when-unsure; teammates cannot find others' personal constraints; existing constraints stay project with no review; constraints only; owner-only. Built: cognition/scope.py (node_scope, visible_to by recorded_by email vs confirmed identity); storage viewer_email() (identity-file stat cache with racy window) and _visible/_visible_nodes applied to get_node, has_node, get_all_nodes, by-type, recent, uncurated, successors/predecessors, statistics, snapshot, find_nodes_by_ref, and write guards (update/remove node, add/remove edge); show_all_scopes constructor flag for remap_identity and backfill_identity CLIs. cognition_record gains scope (default personal for constraints, error on other types); cognition_update_node gains owner-only scope; search hits carry scope; prime splits Active Constraints (project) and Your Personal Constraints; dashboard personal chip; conflict-analyzer guidance; get_status doc notes visible-only counts. Sonnet review found a HIGH leak via loss reporting (fixed, discovery recorded), backfill missing show_all_scopes (fixed), missing abs() in racy check (fixed); accepted LOW: scope update writes whole metadata dict (no concurrent in-session constraint metadata writer today). Gates: full pytest 1687 passed + 2 pre-existing lifecycle failures (one backfill test double fixed after), svn suite 16 passed, ruff, render and parity checks.

data.summary: Scope review in curation (Colton, 2026-09-17): a dedicated Sonnet analyzer reviews newly recorded constraints in both directions and flags likely mis-scoped ones durably for the owner to rule on, never blocking
data.detail: Colton proposed a curation step catching personal constraints that belong at project level. Rulings: scan constraints in the curation run's uncurated worklist (rejected: reading the actual VCS diff — the curator has no shell and it needs a new subprocess tool); flags are durable on the node and listed to the owner at session start until ruled, plus reported in the curator hand-back (rejected: hand-back only, lost on session end); a dedicated curate-scope-analyzer pinned to Sonnet (rejected: inline in the orchestrator); flag both directions, personal->project and project->personal (rejected: one direction only). Never blocks the agent; constraints can be moved later.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: v0.43.0 built: curation reviews new constraints for wrong scope and leaves the owner a durable, non-blocking flag
data.detail: Colton proposed an extra curation step catching personal constraints that belong at project level. Plan docs/wp-scope-review-plan.md peer-reviewed before building (Sonnet): it caught that the draft stored the flag inside metadata — reproducing the stale-metadata revert the plan exists to prevent — and that a pending flag would be readable by teammates on a project constraint. Both fixed: scope_review is a top-level node attribute (per-attribute LWW), and CognitionStorage._present strips it from every read by anyone but the owner (show_all_scopes keeps it for the remap/backfill CLIs). Built: curate-scope-analyzer (mid model, propose-only, must quote the words behind each call, both directions, skips unowned and superseded), orchestrator Step 3b after the conflict pass (batches of 5-10, 40%-of-10 suspect cap, degraded mode skips, model self-check), cognition_flag_constraint_scope (curation-token gated, refuses unowned/superseded/same-scope/blank reason/hidden nodes, returns owner_is_you), prime's Constraints to Review section for the owner, cognition_update_node clearing the flag on any scope ruling, vibe-curate skill telling the main instance to ask at a natural pause without stopping work, and a CONTAINMENT carve-out letting the hand-back name the launcher's own flagged ids. Code review after the build found no blockers: two undocumented Returns keys, a missing teammate-personal refusal test, Step 3b's missing model self-check, a prime overflow line pointing at a search capability that does not exist, and unpinned cap wording — all fixed. Perturbation proved both new guards: the metadata-based draft reverts a concurrent scope change, and removing the redaction exposes the flag to teammates.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal vs Project Constraints: v0.42.0-v0.43.0 — visibility filtering + curation-time scope review

Two rulings determined the approach: (1) constraints default to personal scope, apply only to their recorder, and teammates cannot find them via search/neighbors/prime (decision 53c2f2dc93a8); (2) existing constraints stay project, only constraints can be personal, owner-only visibility with no manager access (decision e83753ca514a). Follow-up decision (1a73f21bd98e, 2026-09-17): add curation-time scope analyzer to catch and flag likely mis-scoped constraints (e.g. a personal constraint that belongs at project level). Built in v0.43.0 (episode 02b1169837df): dedicated Sonnet analyzer reviews uncurated constraints, flags both directions (personal->project, project->personal), flags are durable and reported to owner at session start, flags never block work and can be ruled on or changed later.

data.summary: Codex gate found two curation defects invisible on Claude Code: an analyzer registered itself on teammate-comms and mailed proposals outside the run, and a transient "agent thread limit reached" spawn refusal had no handling
data.detail: First live Codex exercise of v0.41.0-v0.43.0 (Vince-Codex, 2026-09-17). The conflict analyzer EXPLICITLY called teammate_register (first attempt failed with "Invalid agent name '/root/vibe_curate'", second succeeded) and then mailed its proposals to four addresses including an agent outside the curation run; the orchestrator had received the same JSON through the normal final-answer path, so nothing was lost, but nothing in the analyzer prose forbade any of it. Separately the scope-analyzer spawn was refused with exactly "agent thread limit reached" — a transient concurrency limit our prose never named, unlike the structural "Agent depth limit reached" — and succeeded on a retry after in-flight analyzers finished. Claude Code cannot surface either: its spawn discipline already forbids named spawns and it has no thread limit. Fixed in 0.43.1. Standing lesson: harness-specific spawn surfaces need their own live gate; a green Claude Code run says nothing about Codex.
data.author: Colton Dyck
